biggest_catch: Application requires rigorous vetting and training — and most tutor roles are scheduled shifts, not pure on-demand gigs.
catches: Paper tutors go through rigorous vetting, testing, and training before approval.
Most tutor roles require consistent weekly availability (e.g. 10+ hours/week) and scheduled shifts.
Students come through school partnerships — volume depends on program demand.
Pay is hourly and role-dependent; nothing guaranteed.

c1.evidence: Paper's official tutor-jobs page (paper.co/tutor-jobs) states: 'All you need is a laptop or computer and reliable internet.' and 'You'll get extensive training to help students succeed, chances to collaborate with fellow tutors, and ongoing mentorship from a dedicated tutor success team.' Tutors provide 24/7 1-on-1 live-chat tutoring and essay review through school partnerships — a live, provider-owned deal channel.

c2.evidence: Official pages describe hourly tutor roles with pay varying by role — variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: apply to be a Paper tutor, complete vetting and training, get mentored by the tutor success team, take student sessions.

c4.evidence: The official 'Apply to be a Paper tutor' flow has no fee mentioned; Paper provides the training itself.

eligibility: Undergraduate degree (or in progress) in a relevant field with essay-review/tutoring experience and consistent weekly availability.
notes: Scenario: online tutoring via school partnerships. Paper gives students unlimited 24/7 access to vetted tutors; tutors deliver live-chat sessions and essay reviews. Application is a job-like process with vetting and training. Pay is hourly and varies by role — variable, never guaranteed.
